title: Texas's 9th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The race for Texas's 9th Congressional District is an open-seat contest following mid-decade redistricting that redrew the map to favor Republicans. The district, previously held for over 20 years by Democrat Al Green (who is now running in the neighboring 18th District), now encompasses eastern Harris County and all of Liberty County and would have voted for Donald Trump by a 19-point margin in 2024. Republican nominee Alex Mealer, an Army veteran and former candidate for Harris County judge, faces Democrat Leticia Gutierrez, an environmental justice advocate and government relations director, along with independent candidate Roy Morales, a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel. The Cook Political Report rates the district as 'Solid Republican,' though some analysts see a potential Democratic path if turnout dynamics shift.
polling_note: No general election head-to-head polls between Mealer and Gutierrez were found as of June 2026. The only available polling covered the Republican primary and runoff contests.

candidates.name: Alex Mealer
candidates.summary: Alex Mealer is the Republican nominee for Texas's 9th Congressional District. A U.S. Army veteran and former Explosive Ordnance Disposal officer who served in Afghanistan, she holds a BS from West Point and a joint JD/MBA from Harvard Law School and Harvard Business School. Mealer was the 2022 Republican nominee for Harris County Judge, losing narrowly to Democrat Lina Hidalgo, and later served as Public Safety Chair on the METRO Board before winning the GOP nomination for this seat in a May 2026 primary runoff.

candidates.name: Leticia Gutierrez
candidates.summary: Leticia Gutierrez is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 9th Congressional District. She is the Government Relations and Community Outreach Director at Air Alliance Houston, an environmental justice organization, and has lived in the district for 45 years. An immigrant raised by farmworker parents, Gutierrez earned a finance degree from the University of St. Thomas-Houston and previously worked in the banking sector before becoming a community advocate focused on environmental justice, children's health, and immigrant rights.

candidates.name: Roy Morales
candidates.summary: Roy Morales is an independent candidate running for Texas's 9th Congressional District. He is a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel with a background in technology, cybersecurity, and emergency management. Morales served as a Harris County Department of Education school trustee from 2007 to 2013, was the first Chief Technology Officer of the Houston Emergency Center, and has worked as an executive consultant with Strategic Partnerships, Inc.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race (0 polls), so the forecast relies entirely on structural and contextual factors. The district was redrawn via mid-decade redistricting to favor Republicans and would have voted for Trump by approximately 19 points in 2024, giving it a very strong GOP baseline. Cook Political Report rates it 'Solid Republican.' Alex Mealer is a credible Republican nominee with prior countywide campaign experience (narrow loss in 2022 Harris County Judge race). Leticia Gutierrez, the Democratic nominee, has a background in environmental justice advocacy but faces a district where the structural environment is heavily Republican. Independent Roy Morales has some local government experience but lacks the infrastructure or coalition to overcome the district's partisan lean. The open-seat nature adds modest uncertainty, but the district's strong Republican lean and the absence of any polling indicating competitiveness make a Democratic or independent victory highly unlikely. Confidence is medium because the complete absence of general-election polling and the open-seat dynamic introduce unknowns beyond the structural lean.
